findings.title: The version bump to 4 recreates the exact defect this successor exists to close, one artifact over: basedOn.componentSdkContractV4.role now pairs the subject's own fully-qualified name with two bare 'v4' tokens denoting component-sdk-contract.v4.
findings.detail: The field reads: 'Cited. Binds NOTHING. Not applied. Applying v4 is a later D-000 act. g20-fixture-corpus.v4 does not adopt v4 SF-* identifiers as member ids.' The final sentence places the subject's own fully-qualified name and a bare version token denoting a different artifact inside one sentence, which is the precise structure CLAUDE-G20FX-V3-S-1 named at basedOn.d136.role. Read literally, 'g20-fixture-corpus.v4 does not adopt v4 SF-* identifiers' asserts that the artifact does not adopt its own SF-* identifiers, which is vacuous and inverts the field's purpose, namely to record that the corpus does not adopt component-sdk-contract.v4's property set. I verified the referent is real and genuinely distinct: component-sdk-contract.v4 is pinned at c53d541f…, is itself version 4, is CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, binds NOTHING, and defines SF-1 through SF-5; the subject contains no SF-* token at all and its member ids are G20.human … G20.nt7.planAdmission-refused.
findings.theSecondSentenceIsWorse: 'Applying v4 is a later D-000 act' carries a bare 'v4' with no antecedent in the field at all. At v4 both readings are true and coherent: applying component-sdk-contract.v4 is a later D-000 act, and so is recording g20-fixture-corpus.v4, which proposedLaterWork[0] states in as many words ('A later D-000 recording may pin g20-fixture-corpus.v4'). The v3 defect at least gave the reader an absurdity to recover by, since an artifact cannot replace itself. This sentence gives no such signal, so it is strictly harder to disambiguate than the defect the successor was dispatched to fix.
findings.whyThisIsNewAtV4: This is not inherited text that previous reviews passed over. At v1, v2 and v3 the same sentence read 'g20-fixture-corpus.vN does not adopt v4 SF-* identifiers', where N was 1, 2 or 3 and the bare 'v4' unambiguously denoted the only version-4 artifact in scope. The collision is created by this successor's own version bump. The leaf-level v3-to-v4 diff shows this field was edited in this very successor: the speaker was retargeted from 'g20-fixture-corpus.v3' to 'g20-fixture-corpus.v4' while the two bare tokens in the same sentence were left untouched. That is verbatim the mechanism my v3 finding described, 'the field was retargeted for the speaker without being re-examined for the collision the retargeting introduced', repeating one version later on a different citation.
findings.whyItMatters: It is the same defect family and the same field class as CLAUDE-G20FX-V3-S-1: a current-standing basedOn.*.role clause that does not name its referent unambiguously. These role fields are consumed per entry as the candidate's standing explanation of its relationship to one cited input, so a reader of basedOn.componentSdkContractV4.role alone gets one clause whose literal reading is empty and one that is genuinely ambiguous. The artifact also demonstrates that it has the remedy and applies it selectively: seven basedOn entries now carry the disambiguator "Not this artifact's version number." — leftoverJoinV6, sdkJoinV6, g21FixtureCorpusV1, predecessorV1, predecessorV2, predecessorV3, and now d136 and productLaw — while componentSdkContractV4, the one entry that genuinely and numerically collides with version 4, carries no guard and keeps the bare tokens. The anti-collision discipline is once again applied where it is not needed and omitted where it is. The subject's own new failsIf[29] names the defect but binds it to basedOn.d136.role alone rather than to the class, and failsIf[10] is itself one of the three sites carrying a bare 'v4'.
findings.whyNotMustFix: No byte claim is false. The component-sdk-contract.v4 pin is correct at c53d541f…, SF-1..SF-5 really are defined there, the corpus really adopts none of them, DR-125 is not SATISFIED anywhere, and binds remains NOTHING. The authorityClaim's assertion about the repair is scoped to basedOn.d136.role and is true as written, so this finding contradicts no sentence of the subject. A careful reader recovers the intended referent of the final sentence by absurdity. This is a successor-attribution and wording defect, not a semantic takeover, which is the grade Codex assigned to the analogous defect at v2 and I assigned at v3.
findings.repairShape: In basedOn.componentSdkContractV4.role, replace both bare tokens with the fully-qualified name and add the disambiguator the artifact already uses elsewhere: 'Cited. Binds NOTHING. Not applied. Applying component-sdk-contract.v4 is a later D-000 act. g20-fixture-corpus.v4 does not adopt component-sdk-contract.v4 SF-* identifiers as member ids. Not this artifact's version number.' Apply the same substitution at whatIsNotAuthored[3] ('component-sdk-contract.v4 applied, or component-sdk-contract.v4 SF-* identifiers as member ids') and at failsIf[10] ('component-sdk-contract.v4 SF-* identifiers are treated as this corpus applied property set'), since failsIf entries are read standing alone and that one has no antecedent whatever. Optionally generalise failsIf[29] from 'basedOn.d136.role contains a bare version token' to 'any basedOn.*.role or failsIf entry contains a bare version token rather than the fully-qualified artifact name', which would bind the class rather than one instance and stop this defect recurring at the next version bump. Change nothing else: every pin, every fixture, the derivation rule, the platform quotation and all other fields are correct and should carry forward byte-identically.
